doc.title: John LaPorta interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: Opening and LaPorta's switch from alto to tenor
summary: Monk Rowe opens the filmed interview; LaPorta says he no longer plays alto, and recalls owning Jimmy Dorsey's old horn.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: We are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. It’s a great pleasure to have with us John LaPorta, who has a resume that goes on and on, and I would read it except we only have an hour. So we’ll have to see if we can kind of focus in on a few of the many things you’ve done. And you obviously are a clarinet player and a fine alto saxophonist.

I don’t play alto anymore. I did for twenty years. I changed — I was originally a tenor saxophone player, and I changed to help a band out and wound up playing it for twenty years. And then when I went to Berklee I wound up playing in the saxophone quartet there with Joe Viola, and played tenor and I didn’t want to play both. I had Jimmy Dorsey’s old horn.
For years, yeah. And I sold it about twenty years ago to a dear friend of mine that uses it as a spare.
Well you recorded a number of things on alto as well.
Yeah, that was in the time I was playing alto.
